report.answer_text:
ToolShell was a chain of Microsoft SharePoint Server vulnerabilities exploited in July 2025. It let attackers run code on vulnerable servers remotely without signing in. Attackers could steal cryptographic keys to retain access, and Microsoft observed some attackers deploying ransomware. The original chain combined CVE-2025-49706 and CVE-2025-49704; the July response also addressed the critical zero-day CVE-2025-53770 and the related CVE-2025-53771. (content.govdelivery.com)
Who was affected: Organizations running on-premises SharePoint Server, especially servers exposed to the internet. Affected versions included SharePoint Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition. SharePoint Online in Microsoft 365 was not affected. (cert.europa.eu)
Eye Security identified more than 400 compromised systems worldwide—a count of systems, not organizations. Victims spanned government, education, and private industry. The U.S. Department of Energy confirmed that it was affected, including the National Nuclear Security Administration, and said the impact was limited. *The Washington Post* also reported that the National Institutes of Health was hit. (labs.eye.security)
